audit.why: Zoe pokes from 800 on both Paddle Star! and Sleepy Trouble Bubble against a 650 Null Sphere, and Portal Jump on 11/8/5s means she has an escape up almost every time you step in. EVEN 5.5/10 fits 55.53% over 895 games: she owns levels 1-5, Kassadin owns everything after first item.

Portal Jump is a 5s ultimate at rank 3, so Zoe's level 6 spike is small and continuous rather than a cliff; her real spike is Sleepy Trouble Bubble ranks. Kassadin's are 6, Rod of Ages and 16. The spikes[] timings match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states what Sleepy Trouble Bubble actually does to you, and never states the one thing a melee can exploit about Paddle Star!.
audit.why: Riot's text for the bubble: the target falls asleep, 'the target's Magic Resist is reduced', and 'the first source of damage that breaks the sleep is doubled'. That is why stacking MR is the wrong answer here and why the follow-up hit is what kills you — which is exactly what the missingInteractions 'resistances-invalidated' entry flags. Paddle Star! 'Deals more damage the longer it flies in a straight line', so closing distance actively reduces her poke, which is the opposite of how the page frames the range gap. More Sparkles! is also an auto reset after a spell cast — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.
audit.corrected: The bubble's MR cut and doubled-wake damage written into breakdown.cooldowns; the Paddle Star! distance scaling into wants.you[1] and dontsFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint), and dosFull[2].d named no window. packet.defects also reports zero cooldown-sequencing cues anywhere in this matchup.
audit.why: Sleepy Trouble Bubble is 18/17/16/15/14s and Portal Jump is 11/8/5s — the two timers the lane is played on.
audit.corrected: Real numbers and a wait-for-X-before-Y line in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d and dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sixteen lint findings, twelve of them MISGENDER: Zoe is female and eleven writable fields called her 'he/his'.
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists zoe as female; the owner is addressed as 'you', so every third-person pronoun on the page refers to her.
audit.corrected: All eleven pronoun fields fixed, plus two of the four flagged report[] entries (the sweep caps report rewrites at two).
